title: Fppf cover simultaneously avoiding unimodular affine linear forms
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative ring and $n\geq0$. For $1\leq i\leq n$ let $b_i,d_i\in R$ generate the unit ideal, meaning that $r_i b_i+s_i d_i=1$ for some $r_i,s_i\in R$. Put $P(Z)=\prod_{i=1}^n(b_iZ+d_i)$ in the polynomial ring $R[Z]$ [def-weil-polynomial-ring], with empty product $1$, and put $B=R[Z][1/P(Z)]$ [def-weil-ring-localization-away]. The morphism $\operatorname{Spec}B\to\operatorname{Spec}R$ is flat, surjective, and locally of finite presentation [def-weil-affine-spectrum, def-weil-flat-morphism, def-weil-surjective-morphism, def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation]. If $z\in B$ is the image of $Z$, then every $b_i z+d_i$ is a unit of $B$. Thus this single morphism is an fppf covering, where fppf coverings are jointly surjective families of flat morphisms locally of finite presentation. No Noetherian or nonzero-ring hypothesis is imposed.

source.place: Tag 00HQ, lemma-ff-rings; Tag 00HT, lemma-flat-localization; Tag 00HC, lemma-composition-flat. Explicit principal-polynomial-open specialization of the common-translate argument in Conrad Proposition 4.3.1, printed p.130, before (4.3.2).

proof.text: Put $A=R[Z]$ and $L_i=b_iZ+d_i$. By [def-weil-polynomial-ring], the powers $(Z^m)_{m\geq0}$ form an $R$-basis of $A$: the coefficients are exactly the unique finitely supported coordinates. In particular $A$ is free over $R$, so [lem-weil-pbc-projective-module-flat], whose last sentence applies to every free module, makes $R\to A$ flat.

source.place: Tag 051G, lemma-local-artinian-characterize-flat, proof, first sentence (the unrestricted free-implies-flat fact); power basis from the definition of a polynomial.

proof.text: The ring $B=A[1/P]$ is the localization of $A$ at $\{P^m:m\geq0\}$ by [def-weil-ring-localization-away], including when this set contains zero. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-localization-flat] to obtain flatness of $A\to B$. Together with step 1, [lem-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map-comp] gives flatness of $R\to B$. Finally [lem-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map-iff-flat-affine] makes the specified morphism $\operatorname{Spec}B\to\operatorname{Spec}R$ flat.

source.place: Tags 00HT, lemma-flat-localization (1), and 00HC, lemma-composition-flat; scheme translation: morphisms.tex Tag 01U5, lemma-flat-characterize.

proof.text: For finite presentation use the explicit $R$-algebra $C=R[Z,T]/(TP(Z)-1)$. The assignment $Z\mapsto z$, $T\mapsto P(z)^{-1}$ defines $C\to B$. Its inverse sends the fraction $a(Z)/P(Z)^m$ to the class of $a(Z)T^m$. Indeed, equality of two fractions means $P^k(aP^l-cP^m)=0$ for some $k$; multiplying its image in $C$ by $T^{k+m+l}$ gives $aT^m=cT^l$, since $TP=1$. The formulas preserve addition and multiplication and their composites fix $Z,T$ and every fraction. Hence $B\cong C$ has two generators and one relation over $R$. Taking the whole source and target as affine neighbourhoods in [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation] proves that the morphism is locally of finite presentation.

source.place: Tag 00CM, section-localization, fraction equality; explicit one-relation presentation of localization, applied to R[Z].

proof.text: Let $\mathfrak p$ be any prime ideal of $R$. The coefficient reduction homomorphism $A\to(R/\mathfrak p)[Z]$ has kernel $\mathfrak q=\{\sum_m a_mZ^m:a_m\in\mathfrak p\text{ for every }m\}$. The ring $R/\mathfrak p$ is a nonzero domain: if $ac\in\mathfrak p$, primeness puts $a$ or $c$ in $\mathfrak p$, and $1\notin\mathfrak p$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-polynomial-ring-domain] with one variable to see that $(R/\mathfrak p)[Z]$ is a domain. Thus the kernel $\mathfrak q$ is proper and prime: a product mapping to zero has a zero factor. Its contraction to $R$ is $\mathfrak p$, since the reduction of a constant polynomial vanishes exactly when its constant lies in $\mathfrak p$.

source.place: Tag 00FB, lemma-affineline-open, proof, coefficient reduction of a polynomial at a prime; here use R/p directly and its coefficientwise kernel.

proof.text: For each $i$, the equality $r_ib_i+s_id_i=1$ prevents both $b_i$ and $d_i$ from lying in $\mathfrak p$. Therefore $L_i\notin\mathfrak q$ by its coefficient description. Since $\mathfrak q$ is prime, the finite product $P=\prod_iL_i$ is not in $\mathfrak q$; for the empty product this is $1\notin\mathfrak q$. Consequently every $P^m$ avoids $\mathfrak q$.

source.place: Tag 00FB, lemma-affineline-open, proof, nonvanishing coefficient criterion; unimodular linear-factor specialization.

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-localization-spectrum-embedding] to $A$ and the multiplicative set $\{P^m:m\geq0\}$. Step 5 puts $\mathfrak q$ in its stated image, so some prime $\mathfrak Q$ of $B$ contracts to $\mathfrak q$ in $A$ and hence to $\mathfrak p$ in $R$. The contravariant spectrum map of [def-weil-affine-spectrum] sends $\mathfrak Q$ to that contraction. Every prime $\mathfrak p$ therefore has a preimage, which is exactly surjectivity as defined in [def-weil-surjective-morphism]. If $R$ is the zero ring there is no prime $\mathfrak p$ to check, and surjectivity is vacuous.

source.place: Tag 00E3, lemma-spec-localization, image description and inverse prime; Tag 00E2, lemma-spec-functorial.

proof.text: In $B$, write $u=P(z)^{-1}$, which exists by [def-weil-ring-localization-away]. For every $i$, the element $u\prod_{j\ne i}(b_jz+d_j)$ is an inverse of $b_iz+d_i$, since their product is $uP(z)=1$. Thus all required linear forms are units. Steps 2, 3 and 6 give flatness, local finite presentation and surjectivity, respectively; by the definition of fppf covering in the statement the singleton family is an fppf cover. For $n=0$ the unit assertions are empty and $P=1$, so the same arguments apply. They also apply to the zero ring, in which $0=1$ and the unique element is a unit.

source.place: Tag 00CM, section-localization, inverted element and fraction multiplication; definition of fppf covering as stated in the item.
